_note: Difference lines. Each is written only from the two stories' stored howItAppears text for that motif; nothing outside those fields. All unverified. Pairs where either stored entry is marked NEEDS SOURCE get no line, and none is drafted for entries that rest only on Wikipedia (marked DRAFT). Keys are the sorted story ids plus the motif.

differences.cinderella|yexian|lost-object-recognitio: In Perrault's tale the lost glass slipper fits the heroine when it is tried on her foot; in the Ye Xian text she leaves one golden shoe behind, and it reaches the king of Tuohan after cave people sell it there.
differences.cinderella|shakuntala|lost-object-recogn: In Perrault the lost glass slipper identifies the heroine when it fits her foot; in Kalidasa's play a ring, lost while she worships at the Ganges and found by a fisherman in a carp, lifts the curse once the king sees it again.
differences.shakuntala|yexian|lost-object-recognitio: Ye Xian's shoe is left behind at the festival and reaches a king by being sold; in Kalidasa's play the ring, found by a fisherman in a carp, lifts a curse once the king sees it again.
differences.cinderella|rhodopis|lost-object-recognit: In Perrault the slipper is tried on her foot and fits; in Strabo an eagle drops the sandal in the king's lap and the king sends men to find its owner, and Strabo does not say the sandal was fitted to her.
differences.anansi|golden-crab|impossible-tasks: The Sky-god names four captures as the price of his stories (the python, the leopard, the fairy and the hornets); the king in the Golden Crab demands a flower-covered wall and a jewelled garden, each by the next morning, and the crab meets both with the golden rod.
differences.anansi|popol-vuh-twins|impossible-tasks: Ananse is set four captures to buy the stories from the Sky-god; the Hero Twins face deadly nights in the Houses of Blade, Cold, Jaguars, Fire and Bats, and a ball game, set by the lords of Xibalba.
differences.golden-crab|popol-vuh-twins|impossible-t: The king in the Golden Crab sets two overnight building demands, a flower-covered wall and a jewelled garden; the lords of Xibalba set the twins deadly nights in houses of blade, cold, jaguars, fire and bats, and a ball game.
differences.anansi|vasilisa|impossible-tasks: Ananse must bring the Sky-god a python, a leopard, a fairy and hornets; Vasilisa is set household work by Baba Yaga (cleaning, cooking, sifting oats, sorting hay, making poppy-oil), which her doll helps her finish.
differences.golden-crab|vasilisa|impossible-tasks: In the Golden Crab the king demands a flower-covered wall and a jewelled garden by next morning, and the golden rod provides them; Baba Yaga sets Vasilisa household tasks, which the doll helps her finish.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|vasilisa|impossible-task: The twins' tasks are deadly trials in the lords' houses and a ball game; Vasilisa's are Baba Yaga's household chores (courtyard, cooking, oats, hay, poppy-oil), finished with her doll's help.
differences.rhodopis|shakuntala|lost-object-recognit: In Strabo the king sends men to find the owner of the sandal an eagle dropped, and she is found at Naucratis, with no mention of fitting it to her foot; in Kalidasa's play the ring that lifts the curse is lost at the Ganges and found by a fisherman in a carp.
differences.one-hand-girl|popol-vuh-twins|reversal-o: The maimed, destitute girl becomes a prince's wife with a house built by the ring, and her brother is banished; in the Popol Vuh it is the lords of Xibalba who fall, sacrificed and told they will never again be great.
differences.one-hand-girl|rhodopis|reversal-of-fortu: The girl in the Swahili tale rises from destitution and maiming to a prince's wife; in Strabo a courtesan becomes the king's wife, and in Herodotus a Thracian slave, ransomed by Charaxus, grows rich in Egypt.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|rhodopis|reversal-of-for: The reversal falls on the lords of Xibalba, who are sacrificed after thinking the twins defeated; in the Rhodopis accounts it lifts the heroine, a courtesan who becomes the king's wife in Strabo, a slave who grows rich in Herodotus.
differences.one-hand-girl|vasilisa|reversal-of-fortu: The Swahili girl goes from destitute and maimed to a prince's wife, and her brother is banished; Vasilisa goes from persecuted orphan to wife of the Tsar, in the version read.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|vasilisa|reversal-of-for: The twins' reversal is the downfall of the lords of Xibalba, sacrificed and told they will never again be great; Vasilisa's is her own rise from persecuted orphan to wife of the Tsar.
differences.rhodopis|vasilisa|reversal-of-fortune: Rhodopis rises to be the king's wife in Strabo, or grows rich in Egypt after being ransomed in Herodotus; Vasilisa goes from persecuted orphan to wife of the Tsar, in the version read.
differences.golden-crab|one-hand-girl|separation-and: In the Golden Crab the husband leaves after his shell is burned and the princess finds him in an underground palace; in the Swahili tale the prince is away when his family expels his wife and son, and he returns to find graves prepared.
differences.cinderella|fisherman-and-the-jinni|super: Cinderella's fairy godmother provides a coach, attendants and glass slippers; in the Fisherman and the Jinni the freed jinni only leads the fisherman to a tarn where he catches four coloured fish that earn him payment.
differences.cinderella|golden-crab|supernatural-assi: A fairy godmother provides Cinderella's coach, attendants and slippers; in the Golden Crab a golden rod produces the wall and garden overnight, and a servant supplies golden garments and armour.
differences.cinderella|momotaro|supernatural-assista: Cinderella's help is a fairy godmother's magic; Momotaro's is a dog, a monkey and a pheasant who join him after each is given a millet dumpling.
differences.cinderella|one-hand-girl|supernatural-as: A fairy godmother magically provides Cinderella's coach and slippers; in the Swahili tale a sheltered snake leads the girl home, where her hand is restored, and its father's ring can produce food, clothing or a house.
differences.cinderella|popol-vuh-twins|supernatural-: Cinderella is helped by one fairy godmother's magic; the twins are helped by animals, such as ants that steal flowers, and by an insect that is really a hair from Hunahpu's knee.
differences.cinderella|vasilisa|supernatural-assista: Cinderella's godmother is a fairy who provides a coach and slippers; Vasilisa's helper is the doll her mother gave her, which does her work and produces the loom and linen.
differences.cinderella|yexian|supernatural-assistanc: Cinderella's help comes from a fairy godmother; Ye Xian's comes from the bones of her dead fish, which grant whatever she asks.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|golden-crab|supe: The freed jinni leads the fisherman to a tarn with four coloured fish; in the Golden Crab a golden rod builds a wall and garden overnight and a servant supplies golden garments and armour.
differences.golden-crab|one-hand-girl|supernatural-a: The Golden Crab's help is a golden rod and a servant who supplies garments and armour; the Swahili girl is helped by a snake she sheltered, which restores her hand and whose father's ring can produce food, clothing or a house.
differences.golden-crab|popol-vuh-twins|supernatural: The crab's golden rod produces the wall and garden overnight; the twins are helped by ants and an insect (a hair plucked from Hunahpu's knee), and Xbalanque calls animals when Hunahpu is beheaded.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|momotaro|superna: The jinni leads the fisherman to a tarn where he catches four coloured fish that earn him payment; Momotaro is joined by a dog, a monkey and a pheasant, who help him defeat the devils.
differences.golden-crab|momotaro|supernatural-assist: In the Golden Crab a golden rod and a servant provide the wall, garden and armour; Momotaro's help is a dog, a monkey and a pheasant won with millet dumplings.
differences.momotaro|one-hand-girl|supernatural-assi: Momotaro gains a dog, a monkey and a pheasant with millet dumplings; the Swahili girl is led by a sheltered snake to its home, where her hand is restored and a ring provides food, clothing or a house.
differences.momotaro|popol-vuh-twins|supernatural-as: Momotaro's animals join him after each is given a millet dumpling and help him against the devils; the twins' animal helpers include ants that steal flowers, and Xbalanque calls animals when Hunahpu is beheaded.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|one-hand-girl|su: The freed jinni leads the fisherman to a tarn of four coloured fish that earn him payment; the Swahili girl's sheltered snake restores her hand and its father's ring can produce a house.
differences.one-hand-girl|popol-vuh-twins|supernatur: A snake the girl sheltered restores her hand and gives her a ring that can produce food, clothing or a house; the twins' help comes from ants, an insect and animals called by Xbalanque.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|popol-vuh-twins|: The freed jinni leads the fisherman to a tarn with four coloured fish; the twins are aided by ants, an insect that is really a hair from Hunahpu's knee, and animals Xbalanque calls.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|vasilisa|superna: The jinni, once freed, leads the fisherman to four coloured fish that earn him payment; Vasilisa's doll does her work, sifting the oats overnight and producing the loom and linen, and Baba Yaga gives her the skull.
differences.golden-crab|vasilisa|supernatural-assist: The crab's golden rod produces a wall and garden overnight and a servant brings golden garments; Vasilisa's doll sifts the oats overnight and produces the loom and linen.
differences.momotaro|vasilisa|supernatural-assistanc: Momotaro is helped by a dog, a monkey and a pheasant; Vasilisa by the doll her mother gave her, which does her work for her.
differences.one-hand-girl|vasilisa|supernatural-assi: The Swahili girl is helped by a snake whose father's ring can produce food, clothing or a house; Vasilisa by her mother's doll, which does the work and produces the loom and linen.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|vasilisa|supernatural-as: The twins are helped by ants, an insect and animals Xbalanque calls; Vasilisa is helped by one doll that does her work overnight, and Baba Yaga gives her the skull.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|yexian|supernatu: The freed jinni leads the fisherman to four coloured fish that earn him payment; the bones of Ye Xian's dead fish grant whatever she asks.
differences.golden-crab|yexian|supernatural-assistan: The crab's golden rod makes the wall and garden overnight, and a servant brings golden garments; the bones of Ye Xian's dead fish grant whatever she asks.
differences.momotaro|yexian|supernatural-assistance: Momotaro's help is a dog, a monkey and a pheasant; Ye Xian's is the bones of her dead fish, which grant whatever she asks.
differences.one-hand-girl|yexian|supernatural-assist: The Swahili girl's sheltered snake restores her hand and gives a ring that can produce food, clothing or a house; Ye Xian's fish bones grant whatever she asks.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|yexian|supernatural-assi: The twins are helped by ants, an insect and animals Xbalanque calls; Ye Xian by the bones of her dead fish, which grant whatever she asks.
differences.vasilisa|yexian|supernatural-assistance: Vasilisa's mother's doll does her work, sifting oats and producing the loom and linen; Ye Xian's fish bones grant whatever she asks of them.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|golden-crab|tran: The jinni turns to vapor to enter a jar, and an enchanted prince is found half man and half stone; the Golden Crab's prince is a crab by day and a man at night, and can become an eagle.
differences.golden-crab|popol-vuh-twins|transformati: The Golden Crab's prince is a crab by day, a man at night, and can become an eagle; the twins appear after death as fish-like people and then as orphan dancers, and at the end rise as the sun and the moon.
differences.golden-crab|sedna|transformation: The Golden Crab's prince changes between crab, man and eagle; in Boas's Sedna the cut-off finger joints become whales and seals and the stumps become bearded seals.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|popol-vuh-twins|: The jinni turns to vapor and the enchanted prince is half stone; the twins' changes follow their deaths (fish-like people, orphan dancers) and end with their rising as the sun and the moon, and their half-brothers become spider monkeys.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|sedna|transforma: The jinni turns to vapor to enter the jar and a prince is half stone; in Boas's Sedna the cut-off finger joints fall into the sea and become whales and seals.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|sedna|transformation: The twins' changes follow their deaths and end with their rising as the sun and the moon, and their half-brothers become spider monkeys; in Boas's Sedna the fingers become whales and seals and the stumps bearded seals.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|yexian|transform: The jinni turns to vapor and a prince is found half man and half stone; in the Ye Xian text the fish bones provide fine blue-green clothing and golden shoes for the festival.
differences.golden-crab|yexian|transformation: The Golden Crab's prince changes between crab, man and eagle; in Ye Xian the bones provide clothing and golden shoes for the festival.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|yexian|transformation: The twins change after death into fish-like people, orphan dancers and finally the sun and the moon; in Ye Xian the bones provide fine clothing and golden shoes for the festival.
differences.sedna|yexian|transformation: In Boas's Sedna the severed finger joints become whales and seals and the stumps bearded seals; in Ye Xian the bones provide fine clothing and golden shoes for the festival.
differences.anansi|fisherman-and-the-jinni|trickster: Ananse traps a python, hornets, a leopard and a fairy with a palm branch, a water gourd, a pit and a sticky doll; the fisherman wins with one question, asking how the jinni fits in so small a jar, and seals it again.
differences.anansi|popol-vuh-twins|trickster: Ananse sets four physical traps for the python, hornets, leopard and fairy; the twins, disguised as orphan dancers, feign sacrifice and revival and persuade the lords to ask to be sacrificed, and the lords are not revived.
differences.fisherman-and-the-jinni|popol-vuh-twins|: The fisherman tricks the jinni back into the jar by asking how it could fit, and seals it; the twins, disguised as dancers, feign sacrifice and revival so the lords ask for it and are killed.
differences.cinderella|one-hand-girl|unjust-treatmen: Cinderella's stepmother and stepsisters set her household drudgery and a bed in a garret; the Swahili girl's brother takes the property, cuts off her right hand, drives her out, and later denounces her to the king as a witch.
differences.cinderella|popol-vuh-twins|unjust-treatm: Cinderella is made to do drudgery by her stepfamily; the twins are abused out of envy by their half-brothers, and the lords of Xibalba killed their father and uncle.
differences.cinderella|sedna|unjust-treatment: Cinderella's mistreatment is drudgery set by her stepmother and stepsisters; in Boas's Sedna the fulmar deceives her and her father throws her overboard and cuts off her fingers to save himself.
differences.cinderella|vasilisa|unjust-treatment: Cinderella is set drudgery by her stepmother and stepsisters; Vasilisa's stepmother's daughters put out the light and send her to Baba Yaga to fetch fire.
differences.cinderella|yexian|unjust-treatment: Cinderella's stepmother and stepsisters make her do household drudgery and sleep in a garret; in Ye Xian the stepmother's mistreatment begins after her father's death.
differences.one-hand-girl|popol-vuh-twins|unjust-tre: The Swahili girl is wronged by her brother, who takes the property, cuts off her hand and denounces her; the twins are abused by envious half-brothers, and the lords of Xibalba killed their father and uncle.
differences.one-hand-girl|sedna|unjust-treatment: The Swahili girl's brother takes her property and cuts off her right hand; in Boas's Sedna the fulmar deceives her and her father throws her overboard and cuts off her fingers to save himself.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|sedna|unjust-treatment: The twins are abused by their half-brothers and call themselves the avengers of their father and uncle, killed by the lords of Xibalba; in Boas's Sedna her own father throws her overboard.
differences.one-hand-girl|vasilisa|unjust-treatment: The Swahili girl's brother takes the property, cuts off her hand and drives her out; Vasilisa's stepmother's daughters put out the light and send her to Baba Yaga to fetch fire.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|vasilisa|unjust-treatmen: The twins are abused by envious half-brothers and have lost their father and uncle to the lords of Xibalba; Vasilisa is sent to Baba Yaga for fire by her stepmother's daughters.
differences.sedna|vasilisa|unjust-treatment: In Boas's Sedna the fulmar deceives her and her father throws her overboard; Vasilisa is sent for fire to Baba Yaga by her stepmother's daughters.
differences.one-hand-girl|yexian|unjust-treatment: The Swahili girl is maimed and driven out by her brother, who later denounces her to the king; Ye Xian is mistreated by her stepmother after her father's death.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|yexian|unjust-treatment: The twins are abused by their half-brothers, and the lords of Xibalba killed their father and uncle; Ye Xian is mistreated by her stepmother after her father's death.
differences.sedna|yexian|unjust-treatment: In Boas's Sedna the fulmar deceives her and her father throws her overboard and cuts off her fingers; Ye Xian is mistreated by her stepmother after her father's death.
differences.vasilisa|yexian|unjust-treatment: Vasilisa's stepmother's daughters put out the light and send her to Baba Yaga to fetch fire; Ye Xian is mistreated by her stepmother after her father's death.
differences.momotaro|popol-vuh-twins|unusual-birth: Momotaro is born from a large peach that floats down a river and is cut open by an old woman; the twins' mother is made pregnant when the skull of One Hunahpu spits into her hand.
differences.momotaro|shakuntala|unusual-birth: Momotaro comes out of a peach cut open by an old woman; in the Mahabharata Shakuntala is the daughter of the apsara Menaka and the sage Viswamitra, left in the forest where birds protect her until Kanva adopts her.
differences.popol-vuh-twins|shakuntala|unusual-birth: The twins' mother is made pregnant when the skull of One Hunahpu spits into her hand; in the Mahabharata Shakuntala is the daughter of an apsara and a sage, left in the forest where birds protect her.
